artists.biography: Carter the Unstoppable Sex Machine (frequently shortened to Carter USM) are an English indie rock band formed in 1988 by singer Jim "Jim Bob" Morrison and guitarist Les "Fruitbat" Carter. They made their name with a distinctive style of power pop, fusing samples, sequenced basses and drum machines with rock 'n' roll guitars and off-beat wordplay-loaded lyrics. They reached the height of their fame in 1992. Over the following years the band took on new members, topping out as a six-piece, but struggled to regain their earlier popularity. They initially split up in 1998 after releasing seven albums.

Carter The Unstoppable Sex Machine.biography: Carter the Unstoppable Sex Machine (frequently shortened to Carter USM) are an English indie rock band formed in 1988 by singer Jim "Jim Bob" Morrison and guitarist Les "Fruitbat" Carter. They made their name with a distinctive style of power pop, fusing samples, sequenced basses and drum machines with rock 'n' roll guitars and off-beat wordplay-loaded lyrics. They reached the height of their fame in 1992. Over the following years the band took on new members, topping out as a six-piece, but struggled to regain their earlier popularity. They initially split up in 1998 after releasing seven albums.

perplexity.description:
Released in September 1993 on Chrysalis Records, Post Historic Monsters is the fourth studio album by Carter The Unstoppable Sex Machine. Marking a departure from the sample-heavy, punk-pop sound of their earlier work, the album sees the band exploring a broader range of musical styles, with Jim Bob taking on more personal and introspective songwriting. The result is a record that blends melodic rock, Britpop influences, and social commentary, while retaining the band’s signature wit and energy. Notable tracks include the singles "Lean on Me I Won’t Fall Over" and "Lenny and Terence," both of which showcase the album’s more mature and nuanced approach.

Post Historic Monsters stands as a pivotal release in Carter USM’s discography, following their chart-topping 1992 – The Love Album. It demonstrated the band’s willingness to evolve beyond their established formula, earning critical acclaim for its songwriting and musical experimentation. The album reached No. 5 on the UK Albums Chart, confirming the band’s commercial appeal while also broadening their artistic scope. Its mix of personal reflection and social observation set it apart from their earlier, more anthemic work, cementing its reputation as one of their most accomplished releases.
